name: @organza/admin
_comment_browserslist: The oldest phone the shop actually uses is an iPhone 7, which stops at iOS 15 — and every browser on iOS is Safari underneath, so ios_saf is the binding constraint. Left unset, Next compiles for its own default of Safari 16.4 and emits class static initialization blocks, which iOS 15 cannot even parse: the chunk dies with a SyntaxError before React mounts and the boot splash never comes down. The other four entries are that era's evergreen releases, so the target set is one coherent generation rather than Safari 15 next to Chrome 111.

scripts._comment_build: The check is part of the build, not a separate step somebody has to remember: syntax the oldest phone cannot parse is a broken app, and it should fail the image build rather than the till.
scripts.build: npm run check:messages && next build && npm run check:browser-target && npm run check:css-target
scripts._comment_check_messages: Asked BEFORE the build, because it reads the source messages rather than the output: a figure written with ICU's `#` takes its digits from whatever the device thinks Arabic looks like, so the same sentence reads differently on the counter screen and on the phone beside it. See shared/scripts/check-messages.js.
scripts._comment_check_css_target: The same question asked of the STYLESHEET: a colour or a length the shop's phones cannot read is not a broken build anywhere else — every desktop browser draws it perfectly — so the only place it can be caught is here, on the emitted CSS. It is what stands between the shop and another morning of buttons with no background.
scripts._comment_test: The admin's own suite (admin/tests): what a signed-in person can see and do in the SHELL, whatever pages their role holds. Not a second copy of the API tests — those run against a live API from backend/. Run it by hand like `npm run verify`; CI only deploys.

_comment_devDependencies: acorn is here for shared/scripts/check-browser-target.js, which parses the built chunks after next build to prove the oldest phone in the shop can still read them. Declared rather than borrowed from Next's own tree, so the check cannot break when a dependency is hoisted differently.
